extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent examiners (prosecution practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements, limits, and examiner practices for requesting and prosecuting prioritized (Track I and PE‑RCE) examination, and for requests to suspend or defer examination under 37 CFR 1.103. Covers eligibility, fees, claim limits, timing, termination, refunds, and related petition remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Prioritized Examination (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must comply with 37 CFR 1.102(e) and the application must be an original utility or plant nonprovisional application. International applications not in the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, design applications, reissue applications, provisional applications, and reexamination proceedings are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing applications (continuation, CIP, divisional) may request prioritized examination but each application must independently meet requirements. Track I (upon filing) is available for original utility or plant nonprovisional applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a). Applications entering national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 are generally not eligible for Track I; a by‑pass continuation may be used instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Filing Requirement for Utility Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is a utility application, it must be filed via the Office's electronic filing system (EFS‑Web) to request prioritized examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Track I the request must be present upon filing and the utility application must be filed via EFS‑Web. For PE‑RCE requests in utility applications, the request must be filed via EFS‑Web.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and Payment Requirements for Prioritized Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon filing the request the prioritized examination fee (37 CFR 1.17(c)), processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)), and, if not already paid, the publication fee (37 CFR 1.18(d)) must have been paid. In addition, basic filing, search, examination, any excess claim fees, and any application size fee must be paid as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any required fee is unpaid at filing, the prioritized examination request will be dismissed unless an explicit authorization to charge additional required fees is provided in the papers; in that case fees will be charged per the authorization and the request will not be dismissed. The Office will automatically refund the prioritized examination fee if the request is dismissed; the processing fee is retained to cover processing costs. Other application fees are not refundable except as provided by other rules (e.g., petition for express abandonment for refund of search and excess claims fees). See MPEP § 1126 for publication fee refund rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Count and Claim Type Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An application requesting prioritized examination must contain no more than four independent claims and no more than thirty total claims, and must not contain any multiple dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment filed after prioritized examination is granted results in more than four independent claims, more than thirty total claims, or adds a multiple dependent claim, the prioritized examination status will be terminated. Applicants are encouraged to file without preliminary amendments but may file a preliminary amendment on filing to reduce claims to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and Filing Conditions — Track I vs PE‑RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Track I: request for prioritized examination must be filed upon filing of an original utility or plant nonprovisional application (35 U.S.C. 111(a)) and must meet completeness requirements. PE‑RCE: a prioritized examination request may be filed with or after an RCE (37 CFR 1.114) but must be filed before the mailing of the first Office action after the RCE; only a single PE‑RCE may be granted in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one request under 37 CFR 1.102(e)(1) (Track I) and one request under 37 CFR 1.102(e)(2) (PE‑RCE) may be granted in an application. If a PE‑RCE is dismissed, applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 or file a new timely PE‑RCE with proper fees prior to the first Office action after the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness Requirements for Track I (37 CFR 1.51(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Track I application must be complete as defined by 37 CFR 1.51(b) with any excess claims fees paid on filing. The application must be filed with an oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.63), the basic filing fee, the search fee, the examination fee, any excess claims fees, and any application size fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a joint inventor refuses to execute an oath or declaration, an application may still be filed with a prioritization request if a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.47 is filed with the application; prioritized status will not be granted if the 1.47 petition is dismissed. If any required item is inadvertently omitted at filing, items submitted on the same day as filing will be considered filed with the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Content and Translation for By‑pass Continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who filed an international application may participate in prioritized examination by filing a by‑pass continuation under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) rather than entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary that the earlier international application have been filed in English to request prioritized examination of the 111(a) application; however, a translation is required per 37 CFR 1.52(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Annual Cap and Potential Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may limit the number of granted prioritized examination requests in a fiscal year (noted cap of 10,000 for FY2012) and may reevaluate or limit requests per Technology Center or per applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office intends to monitor the program and publish statistics regarding its ability to meet program goals. Applicants should be aware the annual cap may change and that acceptance of a request is subject to the cap not having been reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Practices to Maximize Benefit of Prioritized Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should (A) have a good knowledge of prior art and file with a clear specification and a complete schedule of claims from broad to narrow, (B) submit an application in condition for examination, (C) file replies that are completely responsive and within any shortened statutory reply period, and (D) be prepared to conduct interviews with the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase “in condition for examination” aligns with the accelerated examination meaning discussed in MPEP § 708.02(a), subsection VIII.C. Following these practices helps the Office meet the 12‑month goal for final disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution Time Periods and Termination Triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications under prioritized examination, time periods for reply in Office actions are the same as set forth in MPEP § 710.02(b) (i.e., standard periods), unlike accelerated examination which sets a one‑month no‑extension reply. Prioritized examination will be terminated if applicant files a petition for an extension of time, files a request for suspension of action, or files an amendment that results in exceeding claim limits or adding multiple dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon termination, the application is removed from the examiner's special docket and placed on the regular docket according to its stage of prosecution. While amendment increasing claims is permitted, it simply terminates prioritized examination rather than being prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Final Disposition (12‑month goal)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 12‑month prioritized examination goal, final disposition means that within 12 months from the date prioritized status is granted one of the following occurs: (A) mailing of a notice of allowance; (B) mailing of a final Office action; (C) filing of a notice of appeal; (D) completion of examination as defined in 37 CFR 41.102; (E) filing of a request for continued examination (RCE); or (F) abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritized status is not accorded throughout appeals or interferences before the Board nor after filing of an RCE. Upon mailing of a final rejection (which terminates prioritized exam), applicants may amend claims under standard rules (see 37 CFR 1.116). Upon allowance, applicants may submit claim amendments subject to usual limitations (see 37 CFR 1.312).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund Policy for Fees Relating to Prioritized Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a prioritized examination request is dismissed, the prioritized examination fee (37 CFR 1.17(c)) will be refunded automatically if paid. The processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)) will be retained. Application fees (basic filing, search, examination, application size, excess claims) are not refundable under 37 CFR 1.26, although some (search and excess claim fees) may be refunded via petition for express abandonment; publication fee refund possible per MPEP § 1126 if application is not published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination of prioritized examination does not entitle the applicant to a refund of the prioritized examination fee because termination is not treated as payment made by mistake or in excess (see 35 U.S.C. 42(d) and 37 CFR 1.26(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Recommended Form for Request and Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are advised to use certification and request form PTO/SB/424 available on EFS‑Web when filing a request for prioritized examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any item required for prioritized examination is inadvertently omitted when the application is filed, missing items submitted on the same day will be considered filed with the request under 37 CFR 1.102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition Remedies for Dismissed PE‑RCE Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant believes dismissal of a PE‑RCE request is improper, applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 or may file a new PE‑RCE request for the same RCE. The new request must include proper fees and be timely (filed prior to mailing of the first Office action after the RCE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should review stated reason(s) for dismissal and determine that an Office error was made before filing the 1.181 petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Examination (contrast) — Reply Period and Electronic Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the accelerated examination program (distinct from prioritized examination), any reply must be filed electronically via EFS‑Web and the time period for reply is ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS with no extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The accelerated examination objective is completion within twelve months of filing. The form paragraph ¶ 24.03.AE addresses Compact Disc/CRF submissions that are not fully responsive and grants a one‑month period to correct omissions; extensions under 1.136(a) are not permitted for accelerated examination. The form paragraph is limited to applications filed on or after August 25, 2006 that have been granted special status under the accelerated program and should not be used for applications granted special status under 37 CFR 1.102(c)(1) for health or age or under the Patent Prosecution Highway pilot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of Action — 37 CFR 1.103(a) (applicant request for cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a) must be presented as a separate paper, be accompanied by the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(g)), request a specific and reasonable period not greater than six months, and present good and sufficient reasons why suspension is necessary. The Office will not suspend action if a reply by applicant to an outstanding Office action is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to suspend to allow submission of an IDS will be denied as failing to present good and sufficient reasons because 37 CFR 1.97 provides adequate recourse. If requirements are not met expect immediate action per MPEP § 708. Form paragraphs ¶ 7.54 and ¶ 7.56 are used to notify grant or denial of the petition. Only the Technology Center Director can grant second or subsequent suspensions; such approval must appear on the Office letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of Action — 37 CFR 1.103(b)/(c) (CPA or RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a continued prosecution application (CPA) filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (design CPA) or for an RCE filed under 37 CFR 1.114, a request for suspension of action under 1.103(b) or (c) may be filed at the time of filing the CPA or RCE for a period not exceeding three months. The request must specify the period (whole number of months) and include the processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the RCE is filed, it must be in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114 (i.e., accompanied by a submission and RCE fee); payment of the RCE fee may not be deferred. If the request is untimely, lacks the fee, or the CPA/RCE is improper (no filing date accorded, or RCE without submission or fee), the suspension request will be denied and action will not be suspended. If filing date is accorded to a design CPA lacking some fees, the suspension will be processed and applicant is given two months to pay missing CPA fees to avoid abandonment. Use ¶ 7.56.01 to notify denial for improper 1.103(b)/(c) requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of Examination — 37 CFR 1.103(d) Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) in new applications for a period not extending beyond three years from the earliest effective filing date for which benefit is claimed. The request must be filed before the Office issues an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance. A request must include the publication fee (37 CFR 1.18(d)) and the processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for deferral will not be granted unless: (1) the application is an original utility or plant application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or resulting from entry of an international application into national stage after compliance with 37 CFR 1.495; (2) applicant has not filed a nonpublication request under 37 CFR 1.213(a) (or has filed a rescission under 1.213(b)); (3) the application is in condition for publication per 37 CFR 1.211(c); and (4) the Office has not issued an Office action or notice of allowance. Form PTO/SB/37 may be used to request deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Suspension/Deferral on Patent Term Adjustment (PTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(a)-(d) at the applicant’s request will cause a reduction in any patent term adjustment accumulated under 37 CFR 1.703. The reduction equals the number of days beginning on the date the request for suspension was filed and ending on the date of termination of the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider the PTA consequences before requesting suspension or deferral. See 37 CFR 1.704(c)(1) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Incomplete Compact Disc/CRF Submissions in Accelerated Examination (¶ 24.03.AE)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Compact Disc/CRF submission is not fully responsive but the reply appears bona fide, applicant is given a time period of one month (or thirty days), whichever is longer, from the mailing date of the notice to supply the omission or correction to avoid abandonment. No extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are permitted for applications in the accelerated examination program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must be filed electronically via EFS‑Web so papers are expeditiously processed; if not filed electronically, final disposition may occur later than twelve months. Attach a CRF Diskette Problem Report or a Notice To Comply With Requirements For Patent Applications Containing Nucleotide Sequence And/Or Amino Acid Sequence Disclosures and a marked‑up Raw Sequence Listing when mailing the Office action. This form paragraph is limited to applications filed on or after August 25, 2006 with special status under the accelerated examination program or under 37 CFR 1.102(c)(2) or (d), and should not be used for special status under 37 CFR 1.102(c)(1) for health/age or under the Patent Prosecution Highway pilot.
